_note: LO QUE HAY EN EL MUNDO, as data. What each landmark type, each street sign and each parcel prop LOOKS like — the same three `switch`es the renderer used to carry as raw Canvas calls. The world says WHERE a thing stands (churchill/world/content.py -> manifest.landmarks / .signs / .parcels); this says what is drawn there, in the same spirit as feriaAssets.json and vehicles.json.
_geometry: Plain PIXEL offsets from the landmark's anchor, +y down — the frame the art was already written in (`ctx.fillRect(x - 16, y - 8, 32, 18)` becomes `x: -16, y: -8, w: 32, h: 18`). Parts are drawn in order, so later ones sit on top.
_shapes: The finite vocabulary in src/render/c2d/shapes.js, shared with the vehicle catalog: rect, roundRect, poly, fan, ellipse, disc, stripes, stroke, strokeRect, text, label, areaLabel, repeat, grid. Data composes these and never invents one.
_scenes: Three landmark types and seven parcel uses are drawn by SCENE functions rather than from a parts list, because what they do is arithmetic: the estadio clips to a footprint the BUILD emitted, a school sizes its own pavilion count from its lot, the faro's riprap follows a rim the build measured. Their CONTROL FLOW stays in code — but their content does not. Every colour, count, scale and proportion they use is in `scenes` below, so a designer can retint the faro, move its palms or change how many bands its tower has without touching the engine. What stays unreachable from here is only what comes from the WORLD (a footprint, a rim, a residual), and that is edited through the world editor's world layer, which is where it belongs.

kiosk.note: a churchill stand: where a delivery starts. White and ORANGE — the drink stays red, because that is the syrup.

ferry.note: THE TERMINAL IS A PLACE, NOT A BOAT. This used to paint a hull in the middle of the terminal's own streets — a second, fake ferry parked on the asphalt beside the two real ones you can drive onto. The landmark keeps its name pill and nothing else.

church.note: the shared `props.church` building — nave, bell tower, spire, cross — plus the rose window on the tower and the name pill. The building itself is inlined rather than copied, because a `church` PARCEL draws the same one on its own manzana and the two used to be written out in two different files.
church.label: IGLESIA

cathedral.note: the same building, its own word on the pill — stone, grey and larger is the PARCEL's job, not the pin's
cathedral.label: CATEDRAL

hotel.note: the pill takes the SECOND word of the hotel's real name when it has one — `Hotel Tioga` reads TIOGA

park.note: the green space and its fountain are drawn by drawGreenSpace, which reads the landmark's own w/h — only the area label is art. A MARINE park is a scene and escapes to drawMarinePark.

museum.note: neoclassical facade: a portico of five columns under a pediment

pool.note: El Balneario Municipal at La Punta is a SEA-WATER inlet: its cuadra is painted by the living-sea effect (the outline is in W.WATERS) with a boat and swimmers inside, so the landmark only tags it.

port.note: the quay, a gantry crane, and four containers in four colours

sign.note: a gantry sign over the bulevar — free text, no pill

village.note: a cluster of three small houses, each its own colour

highway.note: a route shield with its number set in the display face

anchor.note: a nautical anchor monument on a low round plinth: shank, ring, stock, and two curved flukes
anchor.strokeNote: THE GROUPING IS LOAD-BEARING. Each `stroke` part is one stroke() call, and two calls that overlap composite their antialiased edges TWICE — so merging the shank, the stock and the arms into one path lightens every crossing by ~30 levels. Measured: 384 pixels, all of them exactly where the stock crosses the shank and where the arms meet it. Keep them apart.

parts.note: arms and curved flukes — ONE path, four subpaths, as they were

bridge.note: drawn separately by drawBridge, from the world's own span geometry — the pin adds nothing

_signs: LA SEÑALIZACIÓN, keyed by SignKind. Costa Rica signs to the Manual Centroamericano de Dispositivos Uniformes, so these are the real shapes: an ALTO is a red OCTAGON carrying the word (not `STOP`), a CEDA EL PASO is an inverted white triangle with a red border, and a tope is the yellow-hatched hump every calle de barrio has. Sizes are world px at the game's framing (~20 cuadrículas across), so a sign reads at a glance without swallowing the lane it stands beside.
_signFrame: `turn: true` means the sign is drawn INSIDE a rotation by its own `ang` — the world measured that angle against the kerb, and a bench or a zebra painted square to the screen is a bench in the wrong street. `flip: "side"` adds a half turn when the roadway is on the far side. `extent: [w, h]` switches the frame from plain pixels to half-extents ([k, px] = k·half + px), which is how one caseta serves a 34 px mapped parada and whatever size the civic block asks for.

alto.note: the octagon on its post, and at this size the word is a bar

ceda.note: ONE path, filled white and stroked red. Two parts would composite the border's antialiased edge twice — the anchor's lesson, from the other side.

semaforo.note: the pole-mounted head at the kerb: three lenses in a dark box

semaforo_centered.note: gantry-mounted LATAM signal: pole at the edge, a horizontal arm over the street, one head centred above the lanes

semaforo_overhead.note: the same gantry with a longer arm and TWO heads, for the avenidas wide enough to need one over each lane

speed_limit.note: a PAVEMENT MARKING, not a sign on a post: white numerals inside a white ring, aligned to the lane. `$value` is the world's own limit.

tope.note: el muerto: the hump, in yellow hatching

banca.note: LA BANCA DEL MALECÓN. `ang` is the direction it LOOKS — the world takes the sea's side of the promenade's own normal, so on a wandering coast every bench still faces the water. The respaldo goes BEHIND the seat, which is the only thing that makes a 10 px bench read as a bench from above.

bus.note: LA PARADA — the SAME caseta the civic block's stop uses, inlined from `props`. Which list a parada came out of, the hand-authored manzana or the 87 mapped `highway=bus_stop` nodes, is not something the player can see, so it must not change what it looks like. `side` says which way the roadway is: a stop on the far kerb turns a half-circle more so it still opens onto it.

_props: PIEZAS COMPARTIDAS — a prop that more than one thing in the world is made of, or that a scene stands on its ground. The frame is the CALLER's, exactly as for a landmark: `paintProp` translates to the anchor, turns by `ang`, scales by `scale`, and switches to a half-extent frame when it is given an `extent`.

parada.note: one caseta, drawn the same wherever a bus stops. Measured in HALF-EXTENTS ([k, px] = k·half + px) because the only thing that differs between a mapped parada and the civic block's is its size — `ang` is the street's angle and the shelter's back is uphill of the bench.

church.note: pale stucco nave, a bell tower with a spire tall enough that it reads as a church and not a house, and a bold white cross on top. Inlined by the `church` LANDMARK (which adds a rose window and a name pill) and by a `church` PARCEL (which adds a ground shadow and is scaled to its own lot) — it was written out twice before, in two files.

churchLot.note: the Parroquia standing on its own manzana: the same building on a ground shadow, drawn in the CUADRA's frame (P.ang) and scaled so it fits the lot

statue.note: a figure on a plinth. `P.statue` names the kind; the Virgen stands at her park's edge NEAREST the catedral, which is placement and stays with the world. The two greys are the catedral's own stone — the same masonry across the calle, not a coincidence worth a registry.

_parcels: POR USO: what a parcel is CALLED on the map and what stands on it. The ground colour is a MATERIAL and lives in materials.json (`parcel`), keyed by the same ParcelUse. `pill` is the word a parcel wears when it IS a landmark; `tone` is the ink of its own name; `label: false` means the ground says everything and a caption sitting in the middle of it would cover exactly what it names.
_parcelScenes: SEVEN BUILDINGS STAY IN CODE, and it is the same line the faro, the estadio and the parque marino draw. The catedral, the Casa de la Cultura, the escuelas/kinders/campus, the gasolineras, the kiosco de parque, the río and the arbolado all size THEMSELVES from the parcel's own half-extents through clamps and counts — `Math.max(3, Math.round(h / 12))` columns, a marked court only `if (L > 70 && ph > 22)`, one pavilion per 46 px of frontage, a tree scatter on a position hash. Moving them would mean putting arithmetic and conditionals in JSON, which is a programming language and not a catalog; §12's own `what should not be converted` list says so. What DID move is what is genuinely art: the parroquia, the Virgen and the paradita — and the parroquia and the paradita were each being drawn twice.

scenes._note: Per-scene palette and knobs. The scene function owns the loops, the clamps and the deterministic hash scatter; it owns no colours and no counts.

faro.note: El Faro de Puntarenas on its plazoleta at La Punta. The riprap follows `lm.rim`, which the BUILD measured against the real sand/water edge — that is world geometry and not a knob.

greenSpace.note: A park or a standalone field. A PARK (`ground: false`) has its green painted by the block footprint, so this only adds the perimeter trees and the fountain; a standalone keeps the legacy self-drawn grass rect.

fountain.note: La fuente in the middle of a plaza. Animated off the shared clock, so the ripple count and the jet period are knobs but the phase is not.

pool.note: A landscaped pool — the Balneario and the Parque Marino's tanks. `s` scales the whole thing; these are its unscaled proportions.

stadium.note: Estadio — el rótulo y LA GRADERÍA. The pitch itself is painted in the acera pass (`paintStadiumCuadras`), because it is a colour choice on ground that already exists; the stand is a STRUCTURE that stands on that ground, so it is drawn here.

stands._note: LA GRADERÍA. Built from the stadium's own emitted `footprint` — the traced cuadra, which already follows the real street grid — so it needs no geometry of its own: name a SIDE and it is fitted to that edge. That is the whole reason it can be one asset for two stadiums whose blocks are different shapes and neither is square to the screen.
stands._history: CLAUDE.md, the ROADMAP and water.json all described graderías 'stroked over the block's real acera ring' when `lm.stands`. None of it ran: the build emits no `stands`, nothing read it, and `drawStadium` was eleven lines. This is the first one that draws.
stands._side: `west`, `east`, `north` or `south` — resolved against the FOOTPRINT's own edges, not the screen: the edge whose midpoint is furthest that way. A cuadra here is not square to the screen (the avenidas run -5.4° and the calles 82.3°), so 'the west side' has to mean an edge and not a rectangle's left.
stands._outward: The stand sits OUTSIDE the pitch, on the cuadra's acera ring — that grey band IS a stadium's sidewalk, and it is where a stand physically goes. Drawn before the landmark pill so the name still reads over it.
stands.depthNote: px from the pitch edge outward. A stand deeper than the acera ring would stand in the street.
stands.tiersNote: stepped bands, back to front. More than about seven and they stop resolving at play zoom.
stands.rakeNote: how much narrower each tier is than the one below, as a fraction of the depth — this is what makes it read as banked seating rather than a striped rectangle.
stands._palette: The default is bare concrete, which is what an unnamed cancha has. A stadium with painted seats overrides the two tier colours below — and they alternate, because a real grandstand's seats are laid in blocks.

estadio.note: Estadio Lito Pérez — naranja, los colores del Puntarenas F.C.

estadio_playitas.note: Plaza Las Playitas — blanco y azul.

stands.roofFromNote: where the roofed part starts, as a fraction of the depth. The two tones are split by DEPTH, not striped — front rows in the open, back rows in shade. Alternating whole tiers and ruling a row line every few px both read as a BARCODE at play zoom; each was tried.

marinePark.note: Parque Marino — its green is the cuadra's RESIDUAL after every other lot takes its space, filled multi-ring even-odd. Only the pill is here.

cathedral.note: La Catedral — stone, not stucco, sized off its parcel and facing east onto the calle peatonal. A placeholder for a proper mockup, so everything is derived from the lot.

civicBuilding.note: La Casa de la Cultura, drawn to fill its parcel.

school.note: Escuela / kínder / campus: a swept yard with pavilions along one edge and a marked court when the lot is big enough. HOW MANY pavilions is a function of the frontage, which is why this is a scene.

fuel.note: La gasolinera: a canopy over its islands, with the pumps.

kiosco.note: El kiosco/templete at a park's centre — the Parque Victoria's bandstand.

parkRiver.note: The channelled river through a park's parcel.

lote.note: A SPONSORED lote — a storefront or a billboard. `lo.tone` is the sponsor's own colour and stays dynamic; these are the fixed parts around it.
